title: Club Brugge at San Siro, and Chivu speaks at 8:30 AM ET
description: Inter arrive on no Champions League points after losing at Real Madrid, and the former Inter goalkeeper Yann Sommer comes back to San Siro in Club Brugge's goal.
mast_alt: Nerazzurri Daily Edition No. 41, Monday, October 12, 2026 — Club Brugge at San Siro, and Chivu speaks at 8:30 AM ET

blocks.html: Inter play their first Champions League match of the season at San Siro on Tuesday, against Club Brugge. Cristian Chivu, Inter's head coach, takes the pre-match press conference at 8:30 AM ET today. Inter have no points in the league phase and sit 25th of 36, while in Serie A they are top with 16 points after beating Parma 3–0.

blocks.h3: Chivu speaks at 8:30 AM ET, and kickoff is Tuesday at 3:00 PM ET
paras: Inter trained at Appiano Gentile, Inter's training ground, at 5:00 AM ET on Monday. Cristian Chivu's official press conference follows there at 8:30 AM ET, which is 14:30 CEST. Club Brugge's own press conference is at San Siro at 12:45 PM ET, or 18:45 CEST.
Kickoff is Tuesday at 3:00 PM ET, 21:00 CEST, at San Siro. The Inter site FCInterNews had listed the press conference at 7:00 AM ET, or 13:00 CEST; the club's own time is the one printed here.

blocks.h3: No points yet in the league phase, and 25th of 36
paras: Inter lost their opening league-phase match 2–1 at Real Madrid. Tuesday is the first of their four home matches in the phase.
Shakhtar Donetsk come to San Siro on Wednesday, October 21, and Inter go to Feyenoord on Tuesday, November 3.

blocks.h3: Club Brugge arrive second in Belgium, with Sommer in goal
paras: Club Brugge have won seven of their first eight matches in the Belgian Pro League and sit second with 21 points, one behind Gent. In the Champions League they have no points either, after losing 3–2 at home to Aston Villa.
Ivan Leko, their head coach since 2025, plays a 4-2-3-1 that can become a 4-3-3. Inter's own analysis points to the high defensive line that Aston Villa punished on the counterattack.
Hans Vanaken, the captain, is the creative hub, and Yann Sommer, the former Inter goalkeeper, is in the Brugge goal.

blocks.h3: Sky Sport Italia expects five starters back for Brugge
paras: Sky Sport Italia, relayed by FCInterNews, reports that Chivu will change the side. Lautaro Martínez, the captain and forward, is expected to start, with the midfielders Nicolò Barella and Piotr Zieliński and the defenders Alessandro Bastoni and Manuel Akanji. None of the five started against Parma.
Inter publish the lineup about an hour before kickoff.
blocks.kicker: SKY SPORT ITALIA VIA FCINTERNEWS · OCT 11

blocks.h3: Rohit Saggi of Norway has the match, with a Spanish VAR
paras: FCInterNews reports that Rohit Saggi, the Norwegian referee, has been appointed for Inter against Club Brugge. Carlos del Cerro Grande of Spain is on VAR.
UEFA makes the appointment, and its own page would not load this morning, so it stays under the rust bar.
Henrikh Mkhitaryan, the midfielder, set up the third, and a video review gave the penalty.
